curation.lead:
Terje Rod-Larsen (born November 22, 1947) is a Norwegian diplomat, sociologist, and former president of the International Peace Institute (IPI). He is best known as a principal architect of the 1993 Oslo Accords between Israel and the PLO, and subsequently served as UN Special Envoy for the Implementation of Security Council Resolution 1559 concerning Lebanon. His wife, Mona Juul, is a career Norwegian diplomat who served as ambassador to Jordan and Iraq. Together they occupied a rare position at the intersection of Norwegian foreign policy, UN multilateral diplomacy, and Middle Eastern political networks -- a position that made Rod-Larsen extraordinarily valuable to Jeffrey Epstein.

The relationship between Rod-Larsen and Epstein, documented extensively in DOJ EFTA releases and House Oversight materials, was not merely social or philanthropic. It was a comprehensive exchange in which Epstein provided escalating financial benefits -- a $130,000 personal loan in June 2013 structured through Richard Kahn at HBRK Associates (EFTA02722550), a $250,000 wire to Rod-Larsen's UN Federal Credit Union account in December 2015 (EFTA02477238), direct funding of the 2018 purchase of Drammensveien 42 in Oslo at roughly half market value (EFTA02477777), and a $10 million bequest to his two children, Edward and Emma, in Epstein's will -- while Rod-Larsen provided Epstein with access to the UN General Assembly presidency, Security Council briefings, Middle Eastern heads of state, the World Economic Forum, and the Gates Foundation. Rod-Larsen forwarded classified UN Security Council briefings to Epstein (EFTA02723735), co-hosted diplomatic dinners at Epstein's 9 East 71st Street townhouse with UNGA President Miroslav Lajcak and Brad Karp (EFTA02235763), and introduced fellow Norwegian establishment figures including Thorbjorn Jagland (former Prime Minister and Secretary General of the Council of Europe) and Borge Brende (former Foreign Minister and WEF President) into Epstein's orbit. Epstein referred to IPI's annual Oslo events as the "Oslo play," telling Tom Pritzker there would be "lots of middel east pols around for the oslo play, any specific country interest?" (EFTA02652208).

In February 2026, Norway's economic crime authority Okokrim charged Rod-Larsen with aiding and abetting aggravated corruption (medvirkning til grov korrupsjon) and his wife Mona Juul with aggravated corruption (grov korrupsjon). Police searched their Oslo residence. The investigation focuses on the Drammensveien 42 property transaction, lavish travel including Palm Beach stays, the personal loans, and Rod-Larsen's writing of O-1 visa recommendation letters for young Russian women in Epstein's circle, certifying "extraordinary abilities" for individuals who were often models without academic credentials. Juul resigned as ambassador. Norwegian media described Rod-Larsen as the "spider at the centre of the web" -- a facilitator who funnelled people to Epstein. IPI itself, which peaked at $11.87 million in revenue and $16.37 million in assets in 2014, has declined to $5.04 million in revenue and $6.91 million in assets by 2023, a 58% collapse in its asset base that accelerated sharply after Epstein's arrest and Rod-Larsen's departure in 2020.
open_questions: Was the $130,000 promissory note for the June 2013 Epstein loan ever executed, and was the loan repaid within its six-month term? If not repaid by December 2013, the loan would constitute a gift to a sitting UN official with potential implications under both US and Norwegian law.

What was the purpose of the $250,000 December 2015 wire to Rod-Larsen's UNFCU account? No service agreement, advisory contract, or IPI-related justification has been documented for this payment, making it the most unexplained direct transfer in the relationship.

How many O-1 visa recommendation letters did Rod-Larsen write for individuals in Epstein's orbit, and who were the specific beneficiaries? The Okokrim investigation has identified this as a focus area, but the full scope of the visa facilitation remains undisclosed.

What role did Rod-Larsen play in directing IPI's grant relationships to institutions within Epstein's broader network, and did Epstein exercise influence over IPI's programming, staffing, or donor relationships beyond the documented ghostwritten letters and staffing memo access?

Did Rod-Larsen's forwarding of UN Security Council briefings and Middle East intelligence to Epstein constitute a systematic intelligence-sharing arrangement, and were these materials further disseminated to Epstein's Gulf state contacts or Israeli intelligence connections?
curation.system_role: Rod-Larsen is the paradigmatic case of a diplomat-as-asset: a figure whose lifetime of legitimate diplomatic achievement -- the Oslo Accords, UN special envoy roles, IPI presidency -- created precisely the institutional access, reputational credibility, and network of world leaders that Epstein systematically monetized. Unlike financial figures who paid Epstein for advisory services, Rod-Larsen was the product being offered, trading diplomatic access for personal financial benefit in a relationship that Norwegian authorities now characterize as aggravated corruption.

sections.title: The Oslo Play: Diplomatic Access as Currency
sections.content:
Epstein's internal terminology for his exploitation of Rod-Larsen's diplomatic network was the "Oslo play" -- a phrase that appears in communications with multiple Epstein associates and captures the transactional nature of the relationship. In April 2017, Epstein wrote to Tom Pritzker: "lots of middel east pols around for the oslo play, any specific country interest?" (EFTA02652208). To Jabor Al Thani, a Qatari contact, he asked: "Are you coming to Oslo play on 5th" (EFTA02651487). The term functioned as shorthand for IPI's annual events in Oslo and New York, which Epstein treated not as diplomatic conferences but as networking marketplaces where he could broker introductions between Gulf state officials, Western political figures, and his own financial contacts.

The access Rod-Larsen provided was not abstract. On June 3, 2018, Epstein hosted a dinner at his townhouse with Miroslav Lajcak, the sitting President of the UN General Assembly, arranged through Rod-Larsen (EFTA02246816). Five months earlier, on January 31, 2018, Lajcak had dined at the same address alongside Brad Karp (chairman of Paul Weiss) and Michael Wolff (EFTA02235763). Rod-Larsen co-hosted formal dinner invitations through IPI with his wife Mona Juul (EFTA02592104), lending institutional legitimacy to what were effectively Epstein salon events. He shared UN Security Council briefings directly with Epstein -- forwarding the full text of his October 2013 briefing on the implementation of Resolution 1559 concerning Lebanon, noting he "thought [it] might be of interest" (EFTA02723735). Rod-Larsen also forwarded Middle East intelligence to Epstein, including "Notes on the Middle East" from Omar El Okdah in October 2014 (EFTA02338032), while IPI staff member Richard Nawrot channeled SAMA/Saudi Aramco intelligence through the Rod-Larsen-to-Epstein pipeline.

Epstein leveraged this diplomatic access to serve other network members. He introduced Steve Bannon to Rod-Larsen at a dinner on March 15, 2018 (EFTA02239420). He brought Borge Brende, then president of the World Economic Forum, to his townhouse for a sushi dinner on June 13, 2019 -- exactly one month before his arrest (EFTA02290348). Rod-Larsen had forwarded Brende's contact details to Epstein's staff as early as May 2016 (EFTA02703534). Brende co-chaired an IPI commission and dined at 71st Street with Wolff on September 25, 2018. The dinner circuit Rod-Larsen enabled was not casual socializing but a structured mechanism through which Epstein positioned himself as an indispensable broker between diplomatic, financial, and political worlds.

sections.title: The Financial Architecture of Dependence
sections.content:
The financial relationship between Epstein and Rod-Larsen escalated steadily over at least six years, following a pattern of increasing entanglement that made disengagement progressively more difficult. The documented sequence begins in June 2013, when Richard Kahn of HBRK Associates -- Epstein's financial manager -- emailed Rod-Larsen requesting a bank routing number, account name, and "ability to sign promissory note for this 6 month loan" (EFTA02722550). This $130,000 personal loan was structured with formal documentation requirements, suggesting awareness of its regulatory sensitivity. Whether the promissory note was ever executed, and whether the loan was ever repaid within the six-month term, remain open questions now under Okokrim investigation.

In December 2015, Epstein wired $250,000 to Rod-Larsen's account at the UN Federal Credit Union (UNFCU). The mechanics are documented in EFTA02477238: Rod-Larsen forwarded his UNFCU account details to Epstein via his assistant Fabrice Aidan, and Epstein instructed Kahn with the single word "250k" alongside the bank transfer details. The purpose of this payment has not been established. Its routing through UNFCU -- an institution serving UN staff and their families -- raises the question of whether the payment was structured to exploit the credit union's limited reporting infrastructure compared to major commercial banks.

The most significant financial transaction was the 2018 purchase of Drammensveien 42, an apartment in Oslo purchased by Rod-Larsen and Mona Juul at roughly half market value. Epstein's instructions to lawyer Kare I. Moljord of Arntzen de Besche Advokatfirma laid out the structure: "craft purchase for 18 million to be held for 3 to 4 weeks terje will put up 4 m, m puts up 4 and terje borrow 10m" (EFTA02477777). "M" refers to Morits Skaugen, the shipowner who sold the property and later described the sale as "not voluntary." Moljord handled the transaction as intermediary, corresponding with Epstein under the subject line "Our mutual friend" (EFTA02483682) and negotiating the release of Skaugen's DNB mortgage of MNOK 18. Skaugen signed the purchase agreement on June 22, 2018 (EFTA02572738), and Moljord forwarded the executed documents to Epstein (EFTA02573110). Three weeks before closing, on April 29, 2018, Epstein told Skaugen "I funded" (EFTA02456962), confirming he directly provided capital for the transaction. The final element -- Epstein's $10 million bequest to the Rod-Larsen children Edward and Emma -- ensured that even Epstein's death would not sever the family's financial entanglement.

sections.title: Patronage of the Next Generation
sections.content:
Epstein's control over the Rod-Larsen family extended beyond financial transfers to the direct management of Edward Rod-Larsen's educational and professional trajectory -- a pattern that deepened Rod-Larsen's personal obligation while creating a second generation of dependency. In July 2017, Epstein had David Stem work on Edward's curriculum vitae (EFTA02224747). By September 2017, Edward was working at "the bank" -- an unidentified financial institution -- from which he sent Epstein a "formal apology for my absence from work" (EFTA02620867), a communication whose formality suggests Epstein held authority over Edward's position there.

In July 2018, Epstein arranged Edward's placement in Christie's Chairman's Programme, an elite internship. Edward wrote afterward: "I concluded my week at Christies yesterday afternoon. It was absolutely great. So much useful advice and information. Just wanted to thank you again for this great opportunity" (EFTA02591946). By October 2018, Epstein was personally editing Edward's NYU application essays, instructing him to "change next to the last sentence. Similarly...to I look forward to accessing the cultural resources in New York in order that I" -- to which Edward replied "will do" (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_033416). In January 2019, Epstein connected Edward to Rita Hauser for an NYU admissions recommendation. Hauser told Edward: "I will speak to the Admissions Office on Tuesday and recommend you for early admission" (EFTA02626583).

The scope of Epstein's involvement in Edward's life -- CV preparation, bank employment, Christie's internship, essay editing, university admissions -- reveals something more systematic than patronage. Epstein was functionally managing the career trajectory of a diplomat's son, creating an obligation that operated on the most personal level a parent can experience: their child's future. The entire Rod-Larsen family was bound into the relationship. On May 6, 2011, Epstein arranged a private jet flight from Teterboro, New Jersey, to Bermuda for all four family members -- Terje, Mona Juul, Edward, and Emma -- booked through Flight Options under the AIRGHN2 account on a Beechjet/Hawker 400XP (EFTA02320631). All four passport details were on file with Epstein's staff (EFTA02319920). The family vacation, the career management, the property purchase, the testamentary bequest -- each layer made the next refusal harder.

sections.title: IPI as Institutional Vehicle
sections.content:
The International Peace Institute, headquartered at 777 UN Plaza in New York, served as the institutional platform through which Rod-Larsen's diplomatic network was made available to Epstein. Rod-Larsen served as IPI president until 2020, and during his tenure the organization functioned simultaneously as a legitimate multilateral policy institute and as the formal host for Epstein's diplomatic access operations. IPI events in New York and Oslo provided the venue and pretext for the gatherings Epstein called the "Oslo play." Formal dinner invitations were sent on IPI letterhead with Mona Juul as co-host (EFTA02592104), lending institutional credibility to events that served Epstein's networking objectives.

Epstein's influence over IPI extended to its operational details. Rod-Larsen forwarded internal IPI staffing memos to Epstein, including a February 2019 employee costs memo from Adam Lupel. Epstein also ghostwrote letters on Rod-Larsen's behalf to Bill Gates, using IPI as the institutional frame. In June 2015, Epstein drafted a "Dear Bill" letter inviting Gates to keynote an IPI pandemic conference, which Rod-Larsen reviewed and returned with "I made a couple of minor edits in the below -- is this ok?" (EFTA02497615), confirming Epstein authored the letter. A second ghostwritten letter followed in January 2019, celebrating "years of cooperation with the Gates Foundation" (EFTA02625684). The June 2015 letter was sent after the Gates Foundation had already formally rejected IPI's pandemic conference proposal in March 2015 (EFTA02713880), suggesting Epstein was attempting to bypass Foundation staff by appealing directly to Gates -- using Rod-Larsen's name and IPI's reputation to do so.

IPI's financial trajectory tells its own story. ProPublica 990 filings show the organization peaking at $11.87 million in revenue and $16.37 million in assets in 2014. After Epstein's arrest in 2019, revenue fell to $9.33 million against expenses of $10.09 million -- already deficit spending. The COVID year of 2020 brought revenue down to $3.93 million while expenses remained at $7.62 million, a $3.7 million deficit. A brief recovery in 2021 ($10.77 million revenue) was followed by continued decline: $6.66 million in 2022, $5.04 million in 2023. Total asset base dropped from $16.37 million to $6.91 million, a 58% loss. A KPMG review confirmed $650,000 in Epstein-related donations to IPI between 2010 and 2020, plus $14,158.88 in reimbursement for a Lawrence Summers flight. The collapse was not merely reputational. IPI lost the network effects that Rod-Larsen's Epstein-facilitated connections had generated -- the donors, the speakers, the attendees who came because of the access, not the policy papers.

sections.title: The Norwegian Nexus
sections.content:
Rod-Larsen functioned as the primary conduit through which Epstein accessed Norwegian political and diplomatic elites, creating what has become the most significant corruption investigation in modern Norwegian history. The documented introductions include Thorbjorn Jagland, former Prime Minister and Secretary General of the Council of Europe, whom Rod-Larsen invited to see Epstein in Paris in June 2018 (EFTA02487846). Jagland appeared in Epstein's contacts and guest lists and met Epstein on September 24, 2018. In February 2026, Okokrim found "reasonable grounds" to investigate Jagland for aggravated corruption, examining "gifts, travel and loans" connected to his official positions. Norway's Foreign Ministry requested the revocation of Jagland's immunity from the Council of Europe.

Borge Brende, who served as Norwegian Foreign Minister before becoming president of the World Economic Forum, was introduced to Epstein through Rod-Larsen. Rod-Larsen forwarded a letter to Brende copied to Epstein (EFTA02258982), and Brende co-chaired an IPI commission. The deepening relationship is visible in the dining calendar: a September 25, 2018 dinner at 71st Street with Michael Wolff (EFTA02683653), and the June 13, 2019 sushi dinner -- one month before Epstein's arrest. After the EFTA document releases, Brende acknowledged "several business dinners" and "a few mails and SMS messages" with Epstein during 2018-2019, while claiming he was unaware of Epstein's criminal history. The WEF launched an independent review of Brende. The pattern -- Rod-Larsen makes introduction, Epstein cultivates relationship, gifts and access deepen entanglement -- replicated itself across the Norwegian political establishment.

The Okokrim investigation, announced in February 2026, charged Mona Juul with aggravated corruption (grov korrupsjon) based on her position at the Norwegian Foreign Ministry, and Rod-Larsen with aiding and abetting aggravated corruption (medvirkning til grov korrupsjon). Okokrim chief Pal Lonseth described the probe as "comprehensive and by all accounts lengthy." The investigation found "significant deficiencies" in Norwegian government oversight of IPI grants, including weak oversight and lack of conflict of interest assessments. The scandal's scope -- touching a former Prime Minister, a former Foreign Minister who leads the WEF, a former UN Special Envoy, and a sitting ambassador -- has produced international coverage across fourteen or more countries. Rod-Larsen's lawyer has stated he is "confident the case will eventually be dropped." The O-1 visa allegation -- that Rod-Larsen wrote visa recommendation letters certifying "extraordinary abilities" for young Russian women in Epstein's circle who were often models without academic credentials -- represents a particularly specific form of institutional abuse, in which diplomatic authority was deployed to facilitate Epstein's personal operations.
